message.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    We report an updated constraint on the Solar System quadrupole parameter
                    <a:math xmlns:a="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <a:msub>
                        <a:mi>Q</a:mi>
                        <a:mn>2</a:mn>
                      </a:msub>
                    </a:math>
                    , which encodes the external field effect predicted by modified gravity versions of the modified Newtonian dynamics (MOND) paradigm. Using the dataset employed to compute the DE440 planetary ephemerides and estimating it simultaneously with other parameters included in the planetary ephemerides, we find
                    <c:math xmlns:c="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <c:mrow>
                        <c:msub>
                          <c:mrow>
                            <c:mi>Q</c:mi>
                          </c:mrow>
                          <c:mrow>
                            <c:mn>2</c:mn>
                          </c:mrow>
                        </c:msub>
                        <c:mo>=</c:mo>
                        <c:mo stretchy="false">(</c:mo>
                        <c:mn>1.6</c:mn>
                        <c:mo>±</c:mo>
                        <c:mn>1.8</c:mn>
                        <c:mo stretchy="false">)</c:mo>
                        <c:mo>×</c:mo>
                        <c:msup>
                          <c:mrow>
                            <c:mn>10</c:mn>
                          </c:mrow>
                          <c:mrow>
                            <c:mo>−</c:mo>
                            <c:mn>27</c:mn>
                          </c:mrow>
                        </c:msup>
                        <c:mtext> </c:mtext>
                        <c:mtext> </c:mtext>
                        <c:msup>
                          <c:mrow>
                            <c:mi mathvariant="normal">s</c:mi>
                          </c:mrow>
                          <c:mrow>
                            <c:mo>−</c:mo>
                            <c:mn>2</c:mn>
                          </c:mrow>
                        </c:msup>
                      </c:mrow>
                    </c:math>
                    (
                    <h:math xmlns:h="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <h:mrow>
                        <h:mn>1</h:mn>
                        <h:mi>σ</h:mi>
                      </h:mrow>
                    </h:math>
                    ), representing an improvement of 40% over previous estimates. We also show explicitly that the contribution to the MOND prediction of
                    <j:math xmlns:j="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <j:msub>
                        <j:mi>Q</j:mi>
                        <j:mn>2</j:mn>
                      </j:msub>
                    </j:math>
                    from the Solar System’s largest planet, Jupiter, is at the 0.05% level, validating the approximation of retaining only the Sun in theoretical calculations. With this new constraint on
                    <l:math xmlns:l="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <l:msub>
                        <l:mi>Q</l:mi>
                        <l:mn>2</l:mn>
                      </l:msub>
                    </l:math>
                    , we update previously acknowledged tensions with external galaxy rotation curves, now leading to discrepancies at the
                    <n:math xmlns:n="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <n:mrow>
                        <n:mn>3</n:mn>
                        <n:mo>−</n:mo>
                        <n:mn>15</n:mn>
                        <n:mi>σ</n:mi>
                      </n:mrow>
                    </n:math>
                    level depending on the detailed mass modeling or the subset of galaxies considered. Within the Milky Way itself, the
                    <p:math xmlns:p="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <p:msub>
                        <p:mi>Q</p:mi>
                        <p:mn>2</p:mn>
                      </p:msub>
                    </p:math>
                    constraint imposes an upper bound of only 2% (at 95% confidence) on the MOND boost to the galactic radial acceleration (i.e., the ratio of the observed over baryonic Newtonian acceleration) at the position of the Sun, in strong tension with current observational limits. The updated
                    <r:math xmlns:r="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <r:msub>
                        <r:mi>Q</r:mi>
                        <r:mn>2</r:mn>
                      </r:msub>
                    </r:math>
                    posterior finally confirms that Solar System measurements provide stronger constraints than current wide-binary data on classical modified gravity versions of MOND.
                  </jats:p>
title: Improved constraints on modified Newtonian gravity from Cassini radio tracking data

reference.unstructured: A. Bosma, The distribution and kinematics of neutral hydrogen in spiral galaxies of various morphological types, Ph.D. thesis, University of Groningen, Netherlands, 1978.
NASA Planetary Data System, Cassini Radio Science Subsystem (RSS) Archive, https://pds-atmospheres.nmsu.edu/data_and_services/atmospheres_data/Cassini/inst-rss.html.
